id.description: Stable internal key. Also the filename the build looks for under assets/bestiary/<id>.svg.

name.description: As the books spell it. Bobs name fauna by resemblance — gorilloid, pigoid, bronto — which is exactly what a bestiary has always done.

namedBy.description: Who coined the name, where the text says. Bob named the gorilloids, Mario the dragons, Howard the trout. Omit rather than guess.

system.description: id keyed into data/systems.json. The validator rejects one that isn't there.

place.description: Name of the world within that system, matching a `places` entry in systems.json — Vulcan, Poseidon, Eden. The validator checks it against that list.

role.description: Ecological role as the text presents it, not as a formal taxonomy. Nothing here is a scientific claim.

sapience.description: Whether the books treat this as a person. 'none' needs the text to settle it — Bk1 ch35 says outright there is nothing but animal intelligence behind a gorilloid. 'contested' is for creatures the books deliberately leave open. There is no 'sapient' value: a sapient species is a people, and belongs in the peoples register. The validator enforces that, because filing the Deltans under 'beasts' would argue against the books.

mentions.description: How many times the name appears across the five books. Checked against .cache/corpus.json when it exists, so a number that drifts gets caught rather than believed. It is a rough weight, not a precise statistic — it counts the word, and words are ambiguous.

cite.description: First substantive appearance. Format: 'Bk<n> ch<n> · <POV>, <date>', verified against the corpus like every other citation.

note.description: Our prose, in our own words — never quoted book text. Shown in the dossier.

art.description: Inline SVG for the illustration. NOT hand-edited: the build fills this from assets/bestiary/<id>.svg so artwork can be dropped in as a file. Kept in the schema so the field is documented rather than mysterious.
